title: All-team trajectory reset — playbook + OKR draft (Nov 2025)
content:
Purpose:

Quick, pragmatic playbook to: (1) align leadership and managers on priority shifts for the next 6–8 weeks, (2) propose a trimmed set of company-level OKRs we can commit to in the all-hands, and (3) outline the comms/run-of-show and mitigations for anticipated questions. This is a working draft — aiming to land a final slate by Nov 25 so the all-hands on Dec 2 can present clear asks.

Context / why now:
- Last quarter we shipped several large infra investments (Dedicated autoscale, console tracing improvements) but growth uptake lagged; signal from sales + support shows several customers delaying pilots citing cost and integration snags.
- Engineering capacity limited through Nov due to release freeze then patching; need a short focused quarter to stabilize SLOs and reduce friction before broad go-to-market push in Q1.
- Leadership requests a concise, single-sheet for company to prioritize — reduce cross-org workstreams, pull forward critical operational investments.

High-level recommendation (one-line):
- Run a 6-week "trajectory reset": prioritize reliability and onboarding frictions, pause low-value feature work, and commit to 3 company-level OKRs that materially improve revenue retention and developer adoption.

Proposed Company Objectives (draft):
O1: Reduce production incident surface and improve perceived reliability for customers
KR1.1: P99 API latency under 350ms for 95% of traffic by end of quarter (baseline: 460ms)
KR1.2: Reduce customer-facing incidents (sev2+) by 50% vs last 60 days
KR1.3: Implement automatic fallback routing for top 3 model routes (hosted -> dedicated) with 99% successful fallback rate

O2: Remove onboarding friction and improve first-week activation for developer users
KR2.1: Increase 7-day active rate for new accounts from 24% -> 40%
KR2.2: Reduce average time-to-first-successful-inference (sample app) from 45 min -> 15 min
KR2.3: Ship a new quickstart template + SDK example for embeddings + caching patterns with >25 internal sign-ups by week 3

O3: Improve unit economics on core inference routes without sacrificing quality
KR3.1: Reduce per-token cost for top-5 routes by 12% via batching/quantization suggestions and cache policies
KR3.2: Maintain quality regression delta < 1% on customer eval sets after optimizations
KR3.3: Migrate 3 pilot customers to dedicated reserved capacity with agreed monthly commit

Notes on draft OKRs: these are intentionally lean — we aim for company-level outcomes that directly map to clear workstreams. Each KR should have a single owner (RACI to be added).

Suggested initiatives by owner (working list):
- Reliability blitz (SRE + Serving runtime) — owner: Tom Alvarez
  - Fast path: deploy rollout of improved KV cache eviction policy, targeted tracing for top 10 routes, run chaos tests on fallback routing
- Onboarding + DX sprint (DevExp + Product) — owner: Priya Sharma
  - Fast path: two quickstarts (Node + Python), one-click model selection in console, onboarding checklist in onboarding flow
- Cost/perf pilot (Optimize + Solutions Eng) — owner: Liam O'Connor
  - Fast path: 2 pilot customers, automated analytics to show per-token savings, recommended config export for customers
- Sales/CS alignment play (GTM + Customer Success) — owner: Sandra Kim
  - Fast path: risk signals dashboard for accounts, reactive playbook for customers impacted by incidents, marketing collateral for reliability improvements

All-hands run-of-show (Dec 2) — proposed 45 minutes + 15 Q&A:
- 0–5: CEO framing — why trajectory reset (Aisha)
- 5–12: Exec highlights — 3 slides, one per objective (PM leads)
- 12–25: Demos & wins — reliability demo + onboarding quickstart (SRE + DevExp)
- 25–35: Customer voice (pre-recorded clip or quote)
- 35–40: What we are pausing and why (single-slide list)
- 40–45: Ask to the org + how success is measured (ops cadence)
- 45–60: Live Q&A (moderated)

Pre-reads for all-hands (deliverables and owners):
- 1-pager OKR sheet (this doc condensed) — Aisha (deliver by Nov 25)
- Reliability metrics snapshot (last 90 days) — Tom (deliver by Nov 21)
- Onboarding funnel heatmap + quickstart plan — Priya (deliver by Nov 21)
- Customer risk list & outreach plan — Sandra (deliver by Nov 18)

Comms strategy (short):
- Nov 18: Exec pre-brief to managers (30 min) + manager FAQ doc
- Nov 25: Publish pre-read + dedicated Slack thread + office hours sign-ups
- Dec 2: All-hands presentation + follow-up mail with actions and owner list
- Week of Dec 8: Manager-led OKR breakdown meetings (30–45 min)

Risks and mitigations (quick register):
- Risk: Signal not improving quickly enough -> customers still churn
  - Mitigation: Prioritize top 5 at-risk accounts for hands-on support; new SLA or financial remediation options as last resort
- Risk: Engineering capacity squeezed by urgent bugfixes -> misses on OKRs
  - Mitigation: Capacity hedge — reserve 1 rota squad for incident response; freeze new feature work except critical security/fixes
- Risk: All-hands messaging leaks to customers and causes worry
  - Mitigation: Draft customer-facing FAQ and communication timeline; counsel GTM to control messaging cadence

Decision points for leadership (need by Nov 20):
1) Approve the three company-level objectives and the 6-week trajectory reset window
2) Confirm the pause list — items to stop or delay (starting immediate post-all-hands)
3) Commit headcount/time from specific teams for the reliability blitz (SRE/Serving runtime)

Open questions / items to resolve in next sync:
- What do we classify as "paused" vs "deferred"? (needs concrete acceptance criteria)
- Do we make the fallback routing auto-enabled for all hosted customers or limited to enterprise accounts?
- Should the unit-economics KR allow temporary quality tradeoffs within a 1% quality budget?

Notes to self / rough asks in doc form (informal):
- Follow up with Tom on whether fallback routing requires infra schema changes (ticket?)
- Ask Solutions Eng to pick two pilot customers who are low-risk but representative
- Draft manager script for Nov 18 pre-brief (short bullets + anticipated Qs)

Appendix (quick links):
- Past incident review (Sept–Oct) — confluence:IR-2025-q3-summary
- Sample onboarding funnel export — JIRA:ENG-2321

Bottom line: this is intentionally narrow — we want a visible short-term win set that buys time for the broader roadmap. If leadership approves the intent, next steps are: finalize KR owners, lock pre-reads, and run the Nov 18 manager pre-brief.

-- Aisha
